title: fix(cron): scripts reject recorded creator origin at message admission
body:
Related: #180537
Related: #166518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled script message actions rejecting a matching recorded creator origin at core admission.

## User Impact

Scripts retain the same creator account and origin through preparation and admission. Channel-owned checks still apply: account-bound Telegram deletion still requires authenticated current-conversation binding, which this change does not add.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admission now consumes the already-prepared scheduled policy instead of the bare persisted policy. No new authority, configuration, storage format, or fallback is introduced. Thanks @InsanusMokrassar for the fix and original proof.

## Evidence

- The new production-path regression fails on current-main-equivalent code with `Scheduled telegram:delete requires matching recorded creator origin`; the same test passes with the fix. Matching, missing, unknown, and wrong-channel origins are checked across repeated invocations.
- All 33 focused tests pass across account policy, admission, plugin reload, and script execution. The regression itself took 27.5 seconds on this loaded host; the four-file run took 254.47 seconds including compilation. Targeted cron test typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks pass.
- Independent Codex review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Production +3/-1 (net +2); tests +162/-1 (net +161), removing 340 lines of unchanged provider/revocation coverage from the earlier PR revision. The two production lines retain and expose the policy already owned by preparation; avoiding them would duplicate resolution or broaden the refactor.
- After integrating main, the production diff is unchanged and the regression imports follow upstream fixture cleanup. The linked local install could not rerun the merged checkout: Vitest lacked `@solidjs/vite-plugin`, oxlint lacked `eslint-plugin-solid`, and the type wrapper refused dependencies physically outside the checkout. Formatting still passes; exact-head CI supplies the integrated proof.
- No new live Telegram round-trip: QA broker credentials are unavailable. Prior contributor loopback CLI/Gateway evidence is preserved below and is limited to core admission followed by Telegram's retained provider refusal. Its separate zero-network-attempt wrapper failed on a blocked ancillary catalog lookup; it is not reported as passing.

<summary>Prior contributor proof and limitations at 5f65ebe03dc6</summary>

Related: #180537
Related context: #166518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled script message actions receiving a missing creator origin at core admission even when the job retains a matching recorded origin.

## User Impact

**This fixes the core admission handoff, not end-to-end account-bound Telegram deletion.** The bundled Telegram adapter separately requires authenticated current-conversation binding. A recorded channel/account origin alone does not supply it, so those scheduled mutations remain denied before provider HTTP.

No creator origin or conversation authority is inferred from routing, no account-bound job is upgraded to operator authority, and provider target checks remain unchanged. Supporting account-bound scheduled Telegram mutations needs a separately agreed authority-capture and revocation contract; this PR does not introduce one.

## Why This Change Was Made

Script preparation already resolves the recorded origin into the scheduled policy context. Admission now consumes that same prepared context instead of the bare persisted policy. This completes the core handoff left outside the preparation/cache fix in #176158.

## Evidence

### Synthetic loopback CLI/Gateway evidence — split result

**The requested admission boundary was observed; the proof wrapper remains `FAIL`.** Its separate zero-network-attempt assertion failed on a blocked ancillary plugin-catalog lookup, as detailed below.

At clean HEAD `5f65ebe03dc621f0f6e5b9d0dc621cc48306f5de`, the normal `scripts/run-node.mjs` launcher ran separate Gateway and CLI processes. HOME, state, config, workspace, caches, and the Gateway port were isolated. Only the external Telegram Bot API and model responses were loopback fixtures with synthetic identities and credentials; this is not live Telegram-service proof.

The shipped Telegram poller received the synthetic inbound message, the normal inbound owner allowlist resolved the creator, and the shipped agent `automations` tool created the job through Gateway `cron.add`. No product source was instrumented, no creator origin was supplied as a job argument or injected into storage, and no routing metadata was promoted to authority. After shutdown, a read-only query of the test-owned SQLite row returned these selected fields:

```json
{
  "scheduledToolPolicy": {
    "version": 1,
    "mode": "account",
    "ownerAccountId": "proof"
  },
  "payload": {
    "toolsAllow": [
      "message"
    ]
  },
  "toolsAllowProvenance": {
    "version": 1,
    "source": "final-executable-surface",
    "callerOrigin": {
      "kind": "external",
      "channel": "telegram"
    }
  }
}
```

`channelRequester` was **absent** in the stored provenance.

Redacted command transcript (connection/auth arguments and generated identifiers omitted):

```text
node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <isolated-port> --bind loopback [auth arguments redacted] --verbose
node scripts/run-node.mjs automations run <synthetic-job-id> --wait --wait-timeout 45s --poll-interval 200ms --json [connection/auth arguments redacted]
node scripts/run-node.mjs automations runs <synthetic-job-id> --limit 5 --json [connection/auth arguments redacted]
```

Selected fields from the **actual `automations run` JSON stdout**:

```json
{
  "completed": true,
  "status": "error",
  "completionStatus": "failed",
  "run": {
    "error": "cron script payload failed (internal_error): Error: Error: Delegated Telegram message mutation requires a provider-observed binding to the exact current topic and account.\n    at openclaw-code-mode:user.js:1:7",
    "deliveryStatus": "not-requested"
  }
}
```

The CLI exited 1 because the provider-owned refusal is intentionally retained. Reaching this distinct Telegram check demonstrates that the matching recorded origin passed core admission without granting conversation authority. The fixture recorded **zero Telegram mutation calls after the scheduled CLI-run baseline**, and **zero `deleteMessage` calls in the complete final trace**. Normal synthetic startup and agent-reply traffic occurred before that baseline.

**Failed-check disclosure:** the wrapper still reports `RESULT=FAIL`; it was not relaxed or relabeled. Its stricter zero-attempt assertion detected one `getaddrinfo("clawhub.ai")` call from Gateway plugin-catalog prewarming. The process guard returned `EAI_FAIL` before the real resolver or TCP/TLS/HTTP. No non-loopback IP connection was observed under that guard; allowed IP targets were only the two proof loopback ports. This proves the bounded admission-to-provider-refusal behavior, not zero attempted lookups. Guard self-test wrappers are not reported as green. Public dependencies/runtime artifacts were staged before the final guarded run, so the entire setup/troubleshooting session is not claimed to have been offline.

Both Gateway and fixture were stopped after the run; the checkout remained clean. Build metadata matched the same commit: `2026.10.6-5f65ebe03dc6-2026-10-24T06-56-32.872Z`.

The follow-up regression uses the real `CronService.run` occurrence lifecycle, script runtime, in-process Gateway handler, bundled Telegram adapter, and Bot API client. Only external Telegram HTTP is replaced by the repository fixture; there is no synthetic provider action callback or always-current occurrence predicate.

- An operator-authorized control reaches `deleteMessage` with the expected chat and message IDs. This is a control, not a recommendation to reauthorize an account-bound job as trusted.
- A matching account origin reaches Telegram’s own conversation-binding denial with zero HTTP calls. On pre-fix core code, that same handoff assertion fails at the earlier missing-creator-origin check; with the fix it reaches the provider-owned refusal without granting conversation authority.
- Wrong account and missing, unknown, or wrong-channel creator origins produce no provider HTTP calls.
- Paired controls use the same held alias `getChat` lookup: the still-active occurrence emits the expected `deleteMessage`; disabling the real occurrence before releasing lookup emits zero deletes. The lookup began before revocation and is not counted as mutation I/O.

Provider-proof validation before upstream integration: **5/5 provider-boundary tests passed**, the owning `test-root-other` type graph and `test-root-e2e` graph passed, targeted lint had no warnings/errors, and formatting/diff checks passed. The earlier core regression and 116 selected checks passed for the unchanged original repair at `7b01230e`.

The provider-proof rerun reused a completed isolated repository runtime build (`OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1`):

```sh
OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/cron-script-telegram-delete.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["test-root-other"]'
```

### CI compatibility follow-up — `5f65ebe0`

CI on `b63429da` exposed a real fixture/API compatibility failure after upstream made per-occurrence admission mandatory: the added core regression omitted `occurrence`, causing both a type error and a runtime failure. The branch was integrated with upstream `648528a15470451db1d6b89ad35a829630372ec3`, and the regression now supplies the existing `TEST_SCHEDULED_OCCURRENCE` fixture. No production guard or authority contract was changed.

Before committing this integrated candidate, focused validation passed: account-policy **3/3**, Telegram provider **5/5**, overlapping cron siblings **30/30**, the owning `services-cron` and `test-root-other` type graphs, targeted lint on all six PR files, formatting, and diff checks. These are the local preparation results for the same source now published in `5f65ebe0`. [Hosted CI for this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40069703324) has also completed successfully, including the previously failing `check-test-types-core-5` and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. Security Review, CodeQL, and OpenGrep passed as well.

A fresh canonical independent `autoreview` of all six PR files against that frozen upstream base completed `scoped-clean`, with no actionable P0–P2 findings. It covered the occurrence fixture, hydrated-policy handoff, real-provider denial boundary, and paired active/revoked lookup controls.

The earlier broad changed-path type wrapper, on the pre-integration branch, compiled all 29 graphs but exited nonzero on source-only shard-size budgets (`gateway-root`: 726/720; `infra`: 737/720). This new `test/` file belongs to neither collector. Those limits were not changed, and the broad wrapper was not rerun or reported green after integration.

No live Telegram service or private production state was used. This does not demonstrate successful account-bound scheduled Telegram deletion or resolve its separate provider-context requirement.


</details>
